Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:1:1.hebrew: כל הקדשים שקדם מום קבוע להקדשן - שהיה להם מום קבוע, והקדישן להמכר ולהבא מדמיהם קרבן למזבח:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:1:1.english: All sacrificial animals in which a permanent blemish preceded their consecration - That they had a permanent blemish, and one consecrated them to be sold and to bring a sacrifice for the Altar from their proceeds.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:1:2.hebrew: חייבין בבכורה - לאחר פדיונן, אם ילדו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:1:2.english: [They] are obligated in [the law of] a firstborn - After their redemption, if they gave birth.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:1:3.hebrew: ובמתנות - זרוע, לחיים וקיבה, כחולין גמורין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:1:3.english: And in the gifts - The foreleg, the jaws, and the maw, like completely non-sacred [animals].

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:1:4.hebrew: ויוצאין לחולין - בפדיונן לגמרי, ליגזז וליעבד כחולין גרידי, משום דמעיקרא לא חיילא עלייהו קדושה חמורה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:1:4.english: And they emerge to non-sacred status - Upon their redemption, completely, to be shorn and to be worked like ordinary non-sacred animals, because from the outset, stringent sanctity did not take effect upon them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:1:5.hebrew: והשוחטן בחוץ פטור - אפי' קודם פדיון, דאפי' הוי מומן קל, כגון דוקין שבעין, דלגבי קדשים מיחייב השוחטן בחוץ — הכא פטור, משום דלא חלה עליהן מתחילה קדושה כל כך:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:1:5.english: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt - Even before redemption; for even if their blemish was a minor [blemish], such as cataracts in the eye, where regarding [other] sacrificial animals one who slaughters them outside is liable, here he is exempt, because such [a degree of] sanctity did not take effect upon them from the beginning.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:2:1.english: And they do not effect a substitution - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:2:2.hebrew: ואם מתו - קודם פדיונן, יפדו להאכילן לכלבים, דאין קדושתן חמורה. ותו קמ"ל, דגרעי משאר קדשים שאין נפדין אלא חיין — שיוכלו לעמוד בפני הכהן בשעת הערכתן, דכתיב (ויקרא כז) והעמיד (הכהן) את הבהמה וגו', והדר והעריך (אותה) הכהן וגו':
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:2:2.english: And if they died - [If they died] prior to their redemption, they may be redeemed to feed them to dogs, for their sanctity is not stringent. And furthermore, [this] teaches us that they are inferior to other sacrificial animals, which are redeemed only [while] alive, so that they are able to stand before the priest at the time of their valuation, as it is written (Leviticus 27): “And [the priest] shall present the animal...”, and then: “And the priest shall evaluate [it]...”

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:2:3.hebrew: חוץ מן הבכור והמעשר - שאפילו במומן חלה עליהן קדושה חמורה: דבכור — רחם מקדשו, ובמעשר כתיב (שם): ״לא יבקר בין טוב לרע״, דמשמע: בין תם בין בעל מום — קדוש; ״טוב״ — תם, ״רע״ — בעל מום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:2:3.english: Except for the firstborn and the [animal] tithe - For even with their blemish, a stringent sanctity takes effect upon them: for [as for] a firstborn, the womb consecrates it; and with regard to [animal] tithe, it is written (ibid.): “He shall not inquire between good and bad,” which implies: whether unblemished or blemished, it is consecrated; “good” [means] unblemished, [and] “bad” [means] blemished.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:3:1.hebrew: מום עובר - כמאן דליתיה דמי, וחלה עליהן קדושה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:3:1.english: A temporary blemish - It is considered as if it does not exist, and [bodily] sanctity took effect upon them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:3:2.english: Exempt from [the law of] the firstborn - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:3:3.hebrew: ואין יוצאין כו' - שאפי' לאחר פדיונן אסורין (בהנאה) בגיזה ועבודה, כדמפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:3:3.english: And they do not emerge, etc. - That even after their redemption, they are forbidden (from benefit) in shearing and labor, as is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:4:1.hebrew: ולדן וחלבן אסור כו' - מפרש בגמרא: כשנתעברו קודם פדיונן, וילדו לאחר פדיונן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:4:1.english: Their offspring and their milk are prohibited, etc. - [It] is explained in the Gemara: When they conceived before their redemption and gave birth after their redemption.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:4:2.english: And one who slaughters them outside - Prior to their redemption.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:4:3.hebrew: חייב - כרת. ובגמרא מפרש: בדוקין שבעין, דראוין הן לפנים, ואליבא דרבי עקיבא דאמר: אם עלו לא ירדו. אבל בשאר מומין — לא, דאמרינן במסכת יומא (דף סג:): הראוי לאהל מועד חייבין עליו, אי לא — לא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:4:3.english: Liable - [To receive] karet. And in the Gemara, [it] explains [that this refers] to [animals with] cataracts in the eye, as they are fit for inside [the Temple], and according to Rabbi Akiva, who said: If they ascended [the Altar], they do not descend. But with other blemishes, [one is] not [liable]; for we say in Tractate Yoma (63b): [For that which is] fit for the Tent of Meeting, one is liable for it; if not, [he is] not [liable].

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:4:4.hebrew: יקברו - ואין נפדין, דבעי העמדה והערכה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:4:4.english: They must be buried - And they may not be redeemed, as [redemption] requires standing and valuation.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:5:1.english: The reason that they were redeemed - It refers to the first clause [of the Mishnah].

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:5:2.hebrew: קדושת דמים - פטורה מן הבכורה כקדושת הגוף, דמפרש לקמן מקראי דפטורה מבכורה וממתנות:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:5:2.english: Sanctity of value - [An animal possessing it] is exempt from [the obligation of] the firstborn like [one with] sanctity of the body, as [the Gemara] explains later from verses that it is exempt from [the] firstborn and from [priestly] gifts:

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:6:1.hebrew: קדשי בדק הבית כו' - והני כקדשי בדק הבית דמו, דהם עצמן לא הוקדשו מתחילה אלא לדמיהן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:6:1.english: Consecrated property of the Temple maintenance, etc. - And these are similar to consecrated property of the Temple maintenance, for they themselves were not consecrated from the start except for their value.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:7:1.hebrew: לא - תסייעיה ממתניתין, דקדושת דמים למזבח הוא — דהוקדשו לשם כן שיהיו הדמים קריבין למזבח — והתם הוא דאסור בגיזה ועבודה, משום דמיחלפא בקדושת הגוף למזבח:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:7:1.english: No - [Do not] support him from our Mishnah, for it is [only regarding] sanctity of value for the altar — as they were consecrated for that purpose, that the proceeds should be offered on the altar — and it is there that [the animal] is prohibited with regard to shearing and labor, because it can be confused with [an animal that possesses] inherent sanctity for the altar:

Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:9:1.hebrew: הא - ולדות שנולדו לפני פדיונן אסורין בהנאה בלא פדייה, ומיקרב לא קרבי, דמכח קדושה דחויה אתו, דאמם לא הוקדשה למזבח:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14a:9:1.english: But - Offspring that were born before their redemption are forbidden from [deriving] benefit without redemption; and they are not sacrificed, for they come by virtue of a disqualified sanctity, since their mother was not consecrated for the altar.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 14a:1:1.hebrew: כל הקדשים שקדם מום קבוע להקדשן - לאו בקדשי בדק הבית איירי, אלא בהקדישן למזבח לדמיהן; דאין חילוק בין רישא לסיפא אלא שזה קדם הקדשו למומו, וזה קדם מומו להקדשו. ואע"פ שעובר כשהקדיש בעל מום למזבח, כדאמרינן פ"ק דתמורה (דף ו:), מכל מקום אשמעינן דינו. והתם מפרש: מאי שנא מדקלא בעלמא? ומשני: בריא מילתא טפי — שביק תמים ומקדשין בעלי מומין:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 14a:1:1.english: "All sacrificial animals in which a permanent blemish preceded their consecration" - [The Mishnah] is not dealing with [animals consecrated for] Temple maintenance, but rather with one who consecrated them to the altar for their value; for there is no difference between the first clause and the latter clause except that in that case [the animal's] consecration preceded its blemish, and in this case its blemish preceded its consecration. And even though one violates [a prohibition] when consecrating a blemished animal to the altar, as we say in the first chapter of Temurah (6b), nevertheless [the Mishnah] teaches us its legal status. And there [the Gemara] explains: In what way is this different from a mere date palm? And it answers: The matter is more disgraceful [lit. conspicuous] — he sets aside unblemished [animals] and consecrates blemished animals.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 14a:5:1.hebrew: קדושת דמים מדחה מן הבכורה ומן המתנות - פי' הקונטרס: קדושת דמים פוטרת מן הבכורה כקדושת הגוף, כדמפרש לקמן מקראי דפוטרת מן הבכורה ומן המתנות. וקשה לפי', דהתם פטרינן בפסולי המוקדשין אע"פ דנפדו — מדאיתקש לצבי ואיל, והכא — דוקא בלא נפדו! אלא היינו טעמא בקדושת דמים: משום דכתיב (במדבר ג׳:י״ג) גבי בכור: "בישראל", ובמתנות כתיב (דברים יח): "מאת העם":
Tosafot on Bekhorot 14a:5:1.english: Sanctity of value defers from the firstborn and from the gifts - Rashi explained: Sanctity of value exempts from [the obligation of] the firstborn just like bodily sanctity, as [the Gemara] explains later from verses that it exempts from the firstborn and from the gifts. And this is difficult according to his explanation, for there we exempt [the animal] in the case of disqualified consecrated animals even though they were redeemed, since it is compared to a gazelle and a deer; but here, [it is exempt] specifically when they have not been redeemed! Rather, this is the reason regarding sanctity of value: because it is written (Numbers 3:13) regarding a firstborn: "in Israel," and regarding the gifts it is written (Deuteronomy 18): "from the people."
